title: Novalogix POC: integration & structured-output pulse review
summary: Weekly POC checkpoint focused on SDK integration for function/tool calling and stabilizing structured outputs. Discussed recent test results (latency and schema validation), a small regression in edge-case serialization, KV cache warmup behavior, and next steps including a short benchmark run and security docs handoff.
topics: Structured output schema failures and tolerances
action_items: Carlos Mendez - run deterministic 1k-request benchmark against dedicated pilot pool and paste results to shared sheet - due 2026-03-09

Aisha Khan - circulate the latest security packet (SOC2 + network diagrams + KMS notes) and include contact for compliance questions - due 2026-03-05

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Khan (Redwood AE), Markus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (CTO, Novalogix), Carlos Mendez (Staff ML Eng), Sophie Zhang (Product Lead)

Auto-generated Summary: Weekly sync for Novalogix pilot. Focus on integration, function calling reliability, and structured output stability. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Aisha: okay, hey everyone thanks for jumping on. quick agenda — status from your side, a couple of notes from the SE team on repros, then next steps. priya you good to start?
[01:02] Priya: yeah hi thanks. overall the SDK is in prod-sim environment. integration with our microservice that orchestrates tool calls is mostly wired. we hit an interesting failure where the structured payload from the model occasionally drops a nested field when the user prompt includes a code block, that happened in ~0.7% of calls in last run.
[02:18] Carlos: adding detail — when the assistant returns the tool invocation json, the "params" sometimes serializes as an inline string rather than as object. looks like a double-serialization in one path of our adapter. we tried to reproduce locally but only see it every few hundred calls.
[03:05] Markus: okay that sounds like a serialization mismatch — one common cause is the SDK helpers doing a toString on bytes if the payload exceeds the size threshold; we pushed a fix last week to treat JSON-looking strings as objects if content-type is application/json, but maybe your adapter uses a slightly different header. can you share the exact raw request?
[04:30] Carlos: yeah we'll capture the raw. note: the error shows up more after long conversations, so it might be a KV cache interaction; the runtime sometimes returns a cached prefix response which then passes through a separate serializer path.
[06:00] Sophie: from product: this only becomes critical if it affects our downstream workflows. we saw two customer flows fail in the staging audit. otherwise behavior is fine. timeline-wise we want the core flows stable in two weeks.
[07:10] Aisha: got it. high level — redwood action is to help reproducibility and propose a quick guardrail; customer action is to run deterministic bench and share artifacts.
[08:25] Markus: i pulled logs from the pilot sandbox and instrumented a run that forces long context with code blocks; i see the serializer branch enter a fallback for cached responses at around 200 tokens. hypothesis: when KV returns a cached fragment, we rehydrate and the SDK's function-calling wrapper doesn't re-parse json.
[09:50] Priya: are there suggestions for a short-term fix so we don't have more user-visible failures? i.e. we can roll a safeguard in our adapter immediately.
[10:12] Markus: yes, short-term we can add a defensive parse step: if a field looks like a json-string, attempt JSON.parse with try/catch and fall back to string on failure. it's a bandaid but buys time.
[11:35] Carlos: that seems fine. we'll do that and also capture raws.
[12:20] Aisha: on performance — carlos, you shared last week's numbers. priya any change in latency profile after enabling batching?
[13:05] Priya: batching helped tail latency, but we saw an uptick in median for short interactions. our flows are mixed — some are 8-12 token tool calls where batching creates a 20-30ms wait. overall cost savings were significant though.
[14:30] Markus: batching tradeoff is common — if most of your calls are small, you can lower batching window or set a route-specific policy. we recommended per-route windows in the config we sent. did you try the 10ms window?
[15:10] Carlos: yes 10ms seemed better than 25ms in our tests, median dropped ~18ms. but then throughput dropped slightly on high concurrency runs.
[16:22] Sophie: for product, latency under 150ms median is still our goal for these micro interactions.
[17:01] Markus: with the current Dedicated pilot pool we can tune cpu/gpu pairing. one knob is to pin the model variant to faster quantization — that reduces memory but may slightly affect accuracy. we can run a quick A/B.
[18:30] Aisha: do we have any quality regressions observed from quantized variant in your tests, carlos?
[19:05] Carlos: minimal. most automated evals on our prompt set showed parity for intent classification and tool call correctness, but some edge-case extraction dropped confidence. i'd like to see redwood's guidance on safe quantization profiles.
[20:10] Markus: we'll send a short doc with recommended quantization profiles per workload — conversational vs extraction-heavy. also note the runtime has fallback to a higher-precision variant if a confidence threshold trips.
[21:40] Priya: can we control that threshold? product wants to increase fallback sensitivity for critical flows.
[22:05] Markus: yes it's in the rollout policy — currently per-route. we can expose it as a config and push a sample.
[23:30] Sophie: another thing — telemetry. we want token-level cost and exact function call counts surfaced in our dashboard. are you able to stream that?
[24:10] Aisha: yes console supports token-level breakdown per route and you can forward traces to your datadog or S3. we'll share a sample dashboard link.
[25:34] Carlos: small note on KV cache warmup — first 50 calls in a test showed higher latency. is there a way to pre-warm the cache for known prefixes?
[26:45] Markus: you can seed the KV cache via the admin API; we can provide a script to pre-warm common prefixes from your prompt corpus. that reduces cold-start tail.
[28:00] Priya: perfect. also, security/compliance — we need the network diagrams, KMS integration notes, and retention policy for logs.
[29:15] Aisha: i'll send the security packet today. it will include SOC2 summary, network architecture with VPC peering example, and KMS/HSM integration notes. retention is configurable; we'll note defaults and options for export.
[30:22] Sophie: timeline question — if we run the benchmark by next Monday and results look good, can we extend pilot for full integration?
[31:05] Aisha: yes that's the plan. we can issue a short-extension SOW for 6 extra weeks to finalize integration and run production-like traffic.
[32:20] Carlos: one more reproducible failure detail — sometimes function calling returns additional unexpected metadata key "aux" which our contract doesn't accept; it's typically empty but breaks strict schema validators. is that on your side?
[33:45] Markus: i think that might be from the runtime adding provenance fields when cache hits are composed. we'll trace the runtime path and either stop adding empty keys or document them so your validator tolerates them.
[35:02] Priya: for schema validation we prefer the model output be strict; we'd rather have optional fields documented than injected.
[36:10] Markus: agreed. runtime team will prioritize removing empty aux keys from composed cached responses. i'll follow up with an update ticket.
[37:30] Aisha: back to action items: carlos will run the 1k deterministic test; markus will provide repro and quantization doc; i will push security docs and calendar invite.
[38:45] Sophie: any blockers on our side? not really, assuming we get the pre-warm script and the defensive parse fix into staging.
[40:00] Carlos: on instrumentation: we noticed a small amount of token counting mismatch between our client and your console (about 0.6%). is that expected?
[41:20] Markus: tokenization differences can happen if there's pre- or post-processing on your side. we can provide a tokenization checksum tool so you can reproduce exact counts locally.
[42:50] Priya: ok please share that.
[43:30] Aisha: timeline recap: security packet today, repro and quant doc by Friday, benchmark results Monday, follow-up benchmark review meeting next Tuesday. pilot extension conversation pending results.
[45:00] Sophie: good. also on pricing: if pilot extends we may need a clearer committed usage level to get the reserved capacity discount. can we see a short pricing sketch?
[46:18] Aisha: yes i'll include a draft pricing schedule in the packet — rough numbers for committed GPU weeks and per-token discounts. not final but helps planning.
[47:30] Carlos: minor ask — can the SDK emit structured-event logs when a function call is executed (so we can reconcile)? that would be helpful for debugging.
[48:05] Markus: the SDK already emits invocation events to the console, but we can add an opt-in detailed event with full call metadata forwarded to your webhook. we'll scope that as an enhancement.
[49:40] Priya: ok that sounds useful. any other items?
[50:02] Sophie: no, that's it from me.
[50:15] Aisha: thanks everyone, we'll follow up on the action items. i'll send meeting notes and the security packet later today.
[51:00] Priya: thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
